1.  CALL TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Traffic Commission of the City of Rolling Hills was called to order by
  Chair Wilson at 8:37 a.m. on Thursday, September 24, 2020 via Zoom, in the City Council
  Chamber, at City Hall, 2 Portuguese Bend Road, Rolling Hills, California.

2.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Raine, Virtue and Chair Wilson.
  Commissioners Absent:  Bobit, Margeta
  Others Present:  Elaine Jeng, City Manager
  Vanessa Munoz, Traffic Engineer
  Deputy Tami Bouse
  Captain James Powers
  Jane Abzug, Assistant Attorney
  Kirsten Orler

3.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  MOTION: Commissioner Raine moved to approve the minutes of the November 21, 2019 and
  July 23, 2020 regular meetings. The motion was seconded by Commissioner Virtue.

  AYES:  COMMISSIONERS: Chair Wilson, Virtue and Raine
  NOES:  COMMISSIONERS: None
  ABSENT:  COMMISSIONERS: Bobit, Margeta
  ABSTAIN:  COMMISSIONERS: None

4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  PRESENTATION BY REPRESENTATIVES OF THE LOS ANGELES COUNTY
  SHERIFF’S DEPARTMENT, LOMITA STATION, ON TRAFFIC STATISTICS FOR
  THE CITY OF ROLLING HILLS.

  Deputy Bouse stated that traffic was light in June 2020 traffic due to Covid-19 pandemic. In
  August 2020, Deputy Bouse reported that the Sheriff’s Department received a complaint from a
  resident on Eastfield Drive reporting violations at stop signs along Eastfield Drive. In response,
  the Sheriff’s Department provided more visibility along Eastfield Drive in August 2020.

  Chair Wilson asked Deputy Bouse if the speeding vehicles observed were traveling up the hill or
  down the hill. Deputy Bouse reported that it an even split. The car that traveled at 50 miles per
  hour was traveling up hill on Portuguese Bend Road and coming around the bend near Poppy
  Trail.

7.  OPEN AGENDA - COMMENTS FROM PUBLIC ON ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  NONE.

8.  MATTERS FROM MEMBERS OF THE TRAFFIC COMMISSION

  Chair Wilson reported that he received a letter from resident Clint Patterson, noting that the
  roadway markings at the horse crossing on Georgeff Road near Crest Road E has faded. Two
  years ago, Mr. Patterson requested that the roadway markings at this location be refreshed.
  Chair Wilson stated that he went out to the location but was unable to find the location of the
  faded roadway marking. Chair Wilson asked City Manager Jeng if the referenced location was
  a part of the inventory provided by the Rolling Hills Community Association (RHCA).

  Mr. Patterson reported that the location is on the blind curve on Georgeff Road, at Georgeff Trail.
  Without proper roadway markings, the location is unsafe through a blind curve.

  City Manager Jeng recalled that the referenced crossing was a part of the city’s recent roadway
  stripping project. City Manager Jeng pulled up an aerial view of the location and asked Mr.
  Patterson if he could point out the exact location of concern. City Manager Jeng reported that
  she will follow up on this matter and have the roadway legend refreshed.

  Mr. Patterson expressed appreciation for Chair Wilson and City Manager Jeng and for their
  commitment to address this matter as soon as possible.

9.  MATTERS FROM STAFF

THRU:  ELAINE JENG P.E., CITY MANAGER

SUBJECT:  2 SPUR LANE: DRIVEWAY WIDENING TO 20 FEET PER FIRE CODE
  REQUIREMENTS (RAJEWSKI).

DATE:  March 25, 2021

BACKGROUND:

The property owners at 2 Spur Lane propose to widen the existing 20-foot driveway apron to 29 feet.
The applicant also proposes to widen the existing 12-foot wide driveway to 20 feet. Their application is
currently being reviewed by the Planning Department and a recommendation of the Traffic Commission
is relative to the widened driveway apron and driveway will become part of the Planning Department’s
recommendations regarding the proposed project.

DISCUSSION:

On October 19, 2020, the applicant submitted an Administrative Review application and plans for: a
remodel, 537 square feet addition, re-roof, 738 square feet covered porches, 312 square feet new garage,
demolition, and 7 cubic yards of grading. Staff approved the plans on November 3, 2020.

Subsequent to the approval, the applicant revised the project which triggered the requirement for a
wider driveway by the L.A. County Fire Department. On January 15, 2021, applicant submitted revised
application and plans with the proposed changes to the driveway and addition. The proposed expansion
of the driveway requires approval from the Traffic Commission. The Planning Department had to delay
the applicant’s project approval pending the Traffic Commission’s approval of the driveway.

The City’s Traffic Engineer has reviewed the plans for the proposed driveway apron and driveway. The
Traffic Engineer visited the site on January 30, 2021 prior to the driveway redesign. Staff conducted a
field visit at the subject property on February 26, 2021 and learned that the applicant had already began

  14
 construction on the driveway without approval from the Planning Department or Traffic Commission.
Please reference the attached photographs from staff’s site visit. The applicant was issued a stop work
order and further instructed to wait until the scheduled Traffic Commission on March 25, 2021. The
Traffic Engineer conducted a second site visit to review the constructed driveway and prepared a report.
Please reference the attached Traffic Engineer’s report.

FISCAL IMPACT:
NONE.

RECOMMENDATION:
Consider the proposed driveway and provide direction to staff.

 Memorandum
 TO:  Meredith T. Elguira, Planning and Community Services Director

 FROM:  Vanessa Munoz, City Traffic Engineer

 DATE:  March 15, 2021

 SUBJECT:  2 Spur Lane Driveway

This memorandum is in response to the request by the City to review and provide input on the driveway
improvements being proposed by the resident of 2 Spur Lane. The proposal consists in widening the
main property driveway from a 12-foot-wide driveway aisle to 20-foot wide driveway aisle. The
driveway location will remain the same on the west side and the proposed improvements will widen the
existing driveway 8-feet to the east.

  On March 12, 2021, a field review of existing
  conditions was performed to assess the proposed
  driveway location with regards to existing condition
  and review the adequacy of the sight distance.
  The field review revealed the driveway had been
  widened 8-feet within private property but the
  matching work within the easement had not been
  completed leaving a gap in the connection between
  the property driveway and the street as shown in in
  picture below

The minimum sight distance for this type of
roadway shall be 155-feet for a 25-mph speed
limit.  The existing driveway meets and
exceed  the  minimum  sight  distance
requirement, furthermore the widening of the
existing driveway aisle is a significant
improvement and will provide better access in
and out of the property. However, the lack of
termination to the existing improvement within
the easement poses safety concerns for
vehicles entering and exiting the property. Vehicles existing the property will have to drive onto the
unimproved area creating an unsafe condition.

Based on the field observations and engineering judgement, the proposed 8-foot widening is not
acceptable as presented in the field, to be safe it shall include widening the driveway approach to
match the existing 20-feet driveway aisle. Once the improvements are revised as suggested, the
driveway will be adequate as it meets sight distance, and the widening would be an improvement to
maneuver into and out of the property.
